paper.citation: Nie, X. and Wager, S. (2021). Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Biometrika 108(2), 299-319. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asaa076.
paper.source_locator: Section 6.1, arXiv:1712.04912v4 (6 Aug 2020) PDF p.16, unnumbered Setup D paragraph (no equation number in the source): 'e*(Xi) = 1/(1 + e^{-Xi1} + e^{-Xi2}), tau*(Xi) = max{Xi1+Xi2+Xi3, 0} - max{Xi4+Xi5, 0}, and b*(Xi) = (max{Xi1+Xi2+Xi3,0} + max{Xi4+Xi5,0})/2'. The same paragraph continues: 'Here, mu*(0)(X) and mu*(1)(X) are uncorrelated, and so there is no upside to learning them jointly.'

mechanism.name: Nie–Wager (2021) Setup D: unrelated treatment and control surfaces

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = b(X) + (A - 1/2) tau(X) + sigma eps, eps ~ Normal(0,1), sigma = 1

generation_equations.label: Arm surfaces
generation_equations.expression: mu0(X) = b(X) - tau(X)/2 = max{X4+X5, 0};  mu1(X) = b(X) + tau(X)/2 = max{X1+X2+X3, 0}

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference
Unconfoundedness: treatment depends on X1, X2 through a sum of exponentials; the baseline uses all five coordinates, so confounding is strong
Overlap: e(x) in (0, 1/3] because the denominator is at least 1 + 2 exp(min(-x1,-x2)) > 1; the design leans towards control

properties.notes: Two disjoint coordinate blocks: X1-X3 raise the effect and X4-X5 lower it, each through a rectifier, so the surface is non-differentiable on the hyperplanes sum(X1..X3)=0 and sum(X4,X5)=0. With the source's centred parameterisation the two arm surfaces are mu0 = max{X4+X5,0} and mu1 = max{X1+X2+X3,0}: each arm sees one block only and the two are deliberately unrelated, which is why pooling information across arms hurts in the source and why T-learners do well.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points; a difference of two rectified sums supported on disjoint coordinate blocks.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points; a difference of two rectified sums supported on disjoint coordinate blocks.
truth.derivation: Closed form: tau(x0) is a difference of two rectified sums, evaluated exactly; the second typing implements the rectifier by branching instead of max(). Checked end-to-end, including the arm-wise identities that the centred parameterisation implies: the treated arm must move by +tau/2 and the control arm by -tau/2 when tau is switched on.

adaptations: Dimension fixed at d = 5, the smallest dimension for which Setup D is defined; the source varies d in {6, 12}.

The source writes Y = b(X) + (W - 0.5) tau(X) + sigma eps with W in {0,1}; this package keeps that centred form exactly and writes it as Y = b(X) + (A - 1/2) tau(X) + sigma eps with A in {0,1}. The CATE is unchanged by the rewrite.

Keeping the centring is essential for this design and is therefore not treated as a cosmetic choice: it is what makes the two arm surfaces disjoint. With it, mu0(X) = b - tau/2 = max{X4+X5,0} and mu1(X) = b + tau/2 = max{X1+X2+X3,0}, so each arm depends on its own coordinate block only. A plain Y = b(X) + A tau(X) would leave both arms carrying b(X) and would destroy the unrelated-arms property that Setup D exists to test.
